newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids steady to up again, NYH firms.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids steady to up again, NYH firms.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices were unchanged to slightly higher again Friday in thin trade, with sweltering heat still gripping the East and raising prospects for better utility demand, sources said.

"There hasn't been a lot of actual oil moving yet, but with the heat, utilities eventually will have to buy," said one cash trader, noting East Coast temperatures were expected to warm again next week after a brief cool down over the weekend.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent was quoted a dime higher at about $17.25 a barrel, with August one percent paper little changed at about $17 despite slumping crude.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour also inched up slightly to $18.25 on expectations for better utility demand from the heat.
High sulphurs in New York were steady to modestly higher, with 2.2 percent now talked near $15.50.
At the U.S. Gulf, prices again were stable, with one percent still in the low-$16s and three percent at $14.50-75.
No NYH or USG deals were reported.

New York city gate weekend gas slipped five cents Friday to the mid-$2.50s/mmBtu, or $16.07 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, was three cents lower at $2.25/mmBtu, or $14.18 a barrel.
